summary: Held through the first several minutes of chop (px oscillating roughly -3 to +25) as normal noise around a working thesis, including a couple of small dips that recovered on prior frames. At t=16m the picture changed qualitatively: a clean 6-frame monotonic decay from +19.25 down through +4.75/+4.25/+2.25/-3.25 to -11.25, with the new down-leg showing only 3% giveback (i.e. not bouncing) versus earlier dips that snapped back within a frame or two -- that combination (sustained direction + low retracement) is what separated this from prior noise and triggered the bail. Next time I'd watch giveback% on the active leg as the key discriminator between a dip (high giveback, quick recovery) and a real breakdown (low giveback, persistent one-way drift), and would consider bailing a frame or two earlier once 3+ consecutive frames confirm the same direction with shrinking giveback.
